olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Suppose that the set
$$\{1,2,\ldots,1998\}$$
has been partitioned into disjoint pairs
$$\{a_i,b_i\}\qquad (1\le i\le999)$$
so that for all $i$,
$$|a_i-b_i|$$
equals $1$ or $6$. Prove that the sum
$$|a_1-b_1|+|a_2-b_2|+\cdots+|a_{999}-b_{999}|$$
ends in the digit $9$.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $C_1$ and $C_2$ be concentric circles, with $C_2$ in the interior of $C_1$. From a point $A$ on $C_1$ one draws the tangent $AB$ to $C_2$ ($B\in C_2$). Let $C$ be the second point of intersection of $AB$ and $C_1$, and let $D$ be the midpoint of $AB$. A line passing through $A$ intersects $C_2$ at $E$ and $F$ in such a way that the perpendicular bisectors of $DE$ and $CF$ intersect at a point $M$ on $AB$. Find, with proof, the ratio
$$\frac{AM}{MC}.$$
figure_description: Two concentric circles with tangent construction and perpendicular bisectors intersecting on a secant.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let $a_0,a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be numbers from the interval
$$\left(0,\frac\pi2\right)$$
such that
$$
\tan\left(a_0-\frac\pi4\right)
+
\tan\left(a_1-\frac\pi4\right)
+
\cdots
+
\tan\left(a_n-\frac\pi4\right)
\ge n-1.
$$
Prove that
$$
\tan a_0\tan a_1\cdots\tan a_n
\ge
n^{n+1}.
$$

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement: A computer screen shows a $98\times98$ chessboard, colored in the usual way. One can select with a mouse any rectangle with sides on the lines of the chessboard and click the mouse button: as a result, the colors in the selected rectangle switch (black becomes white, white becomes black). Find, with proof, the minimum number of mouse clicks needed to make the chessboard all one color.

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Prove that for each
$$n\ge2,$$
there is a set $S$ of $n$ integers such that
$$(a-b)^2$$
divides $ab$ for every distinct
$$a,b\in S.$$

olympiad_full_name: United States of America Mathematical Olympiad
statement:
Let
$$n\ge5$$
be an integer. Find the largest integer $k$ (as a function of $n$) such that there exists a convex $n$-gon
$$A_1A_2\cdots A_n$$
for which exactly $k$ of the quadrilaterals
$$A_iA_{i+1}A_{i+2}A_{i+3}$$
have an inscribed circle. (Here
$$A_{n+j}=A_j.$$)
figure_description: Cyclic indexing of quadrilaterals formed from consecutive vertices of a convex polygon.
